purpose: Scientifically substantive, cheaper comparison of trajectory sets preserving declared adapted-OT proximity decisions with an explicit guarantee.
priority_order: Scientific significance and distance from nearest prior art
Conditional/temporal mechanism for avoided or shared computation

scope_change.authority: User permits approximate scores if pairwise relationships are guaranteed, prioritizes scientific weight, and explicitly requests scope reframing after the new update.
scope_change.legacy_solver_objective: Parked, neither achieved nor disproved. Its 0.5% value target and full grid bind only a separately labelled v2 solver claim.

target.objects: Database and queries consisting of probability laws reconstructed from trajectory sets; retain masses, time order and conditional history.
target.reference: D(A,B)=unregularized bicausal/nested OT value V=AW_p^p on the declared finite quantized k-window models.
target.information: Observed paths only. Generator parameters, reference labels and fallback solver calls are not free candidate information; disclose and charge all labels/calibration/oracle access.
target.task_consistency: Fix k, grid/shift construction, horizon, cost, units and normalization within each ranking task. Do not rank heterogeneous targets together. AW_p and AW_p^p preserve ordering only within a fixed p task.
target.primary_decision: Query-relative ordering and top-K retrieval according to D, including ties, unresolved decisions and charged fallback.
target.secondary_decisions: Global ordering of pair distances or clustering need separately frozen metrics and claims; one task does not validate another.
target.not_required: Each value accurate to 0.5%, exact equality with D, or a full all-pairs distance table.
target.population_boundary: No population or application-label guarantee. Changing the reference requires a separate amendment and evidence.

primary.requirement: Every asserted strict comparison or certified top-K membership is valid for D under explicit verifiable assumptions. Unverified cases remain unresolved or invoke charged fallback.
allowed_routes: Direct ordering/distortion theorem with computable applicability test
Valid intervals or monotone-transformation bounds proving ordering
primary.interval_example: U(q,a)<L(q,b) certifies D(q,a)<D(q,b). This implication is elementary; obtaining useful information cheaply is the unresolved contribution.
primary.top_k: Prove every selected item closer than every excluded item, or specify a tie-aware set-valued output. ID tie breaking cannot certify an unresolved strict order.
primary.margin: Preregister margin/near-tie rules. Include unresolved or excluded near ties in reported denominators; stratify by margin rather than silently dropping hard pairs.

alternative.status: Select only by an explicit pre-run amendment, not by substitution after deterministic gates fail.
alternative.requirement: Declare sampling population, error event, confidence, calibration, simultaneous/adaptive-query validity and nontrivial coverage. Empirical correlation or bootstrap intervals alone are not distribution-free guarantees.

insufficient: Ordinary tree-Wasserstein distortion without a bicausal bridge
A lower bound alone used to assert ordering
Resolving everything with uncharged exact solves

mechanism_policy.candidate: Shared support tree or multiple trees with conditional/future-law information, cheap scores and selective refinement; a hypothesis, not a validated construction.
mechanism_policy.known_baseline: Closed-form tree-Wasserstein is prior art. A trie does not enforce bicausality, and edge edit costs need not preserve reference costs.
mechanism_policy.novelty_gate: A new useful relation between representation and adapted-OT decisions, explicit assumptions, adversarial discriminator and avoided work. Generic tree embedding, interval sorting or BRTDP transfer alone is insufficient.
mechanism_policy.representation_scope: Freeze training-only, database-built or transductive tree regime; charge query insertion/updates; held-out reference labels cannot shape the tree.
mechanism_policy.legacy_assets: Joint refinement, structured local OT, Gaussian oracle and rigorous arithmetic are supporting tools. Interaction compression is parked pending independent review, not universally refuted.

evaluation.breadth: A meaningful declared subclass is allowed. General claims must challenge nonmonotone second-order dependence and information-release timing. The v2 grid is a challenge pool, not an automatic v3 gate.
required_challenges: Similar path geometry with different timing of information revelation
Equal current values with different conditional futures, including k=2
Absolute and squared costs unless a restricted claim is declared
Scaling in horizon, paths, database size and query count; T=50 for an eventual long-horizon claim
evaluation.splits: Split processes/trajectory sets into training, development/calibration and held-out confirmation groups. Derived pairs/triplets inherit object groups. Pair splits sharing objects are not independent generalization evidence; distinguish within-family and held-out-family claims.
evaluation.reference_protocol: Analytic/independently verified references on manageable cases. Float DP labels are numerical; overlapping reference intervals cannot establish strict ordering. Large-case guarantees require theory/numerics review, not universal full-DP labels.
primary_metrics: Certified coverage before fallback, unresolved/fallback fractions and final coverage
End-to-end time/work at matched guarantee and coverage
Expensive adapted-OT calls and continuation entries avoided
reports: amortized with database/query counts and break-even
comparators: Strong eligible adapted-OT solvers with early stopping when the decision is resolved; never require unnecessary 0.5% precision
Ordinary shared-trie/tree-Wasserstein, tree-sliced and eligible learned-tree methods
Simple temporal/marginal summaries and ablation removing conditional information
Same refinement pipeline with proposed structural mechanism disabled
evaluation.threshold_policy: Before each probe freeze numerical coverage/risk, material cost-reduction, margin/tie, sample-size, fallback and budget thresholds with rationale. Old v2 experiments do not satisfy these gates retroactively.

completion.scientific_weight_gate_first: Before implementation, state the successful paper-level claim, nearest theorem/algorithm, nontrivial remaining contribution and feasible decisive falsifier. Cheapness alone does not justify a probe.
required: Reviewed guarantee on the correct finite-model target
Structural mechanism with honest cost accounting
Preregistered nontrivial coverage and material matched-guarantee/coverage advantage on held-out data

research_outcomes.relational_research_objective_achieved: All v3 gates satisfied on the declared domain with substantive independently reviewed contribution; does not imply v2 completion or population validity.
research_outcomes.empirical_surrogate_result: Useful correlation/retrieval evidence without required guarantee; exploratory, not v3 completion.
research_outcomes.scoped_negative_research_complete: Substantive reviewed limitation theorem for an explicit representation/algorithm class, access model, target and domain; never inferred from failed probes alone.
research_outcomes.limited_domain_result: Exact coverage and exclusions disclosed; no general claim beyond them.
research_outcomes.direction_stopped_evidence_based: Stop a tested construction with evidence and open questions, not an impossibility theorem.
research_outcomes.legacy_solver_objective_achieved: Requires every original v2 gate, separately evaluated against the immutable v2 snapshot.

orchestration.next_step: One bounded claim/counterexample packet for shared-tree adapted-OT ordering. Inspect overlap before implementation. No automatic P1/P2, W1 overhaul or grid.
task_gate: Is a cheaper decisive check available?
orchestration.routing: Root integrates; one bounded independent reviewer for a concrete claim, one implementer after that gate. No quota of agents or hypotheses.
orchestration.validator_boundary: workflow.py check-report supports v1/v2 numerical solver screening only; v3 returns NOT_READY. A ranking validator requires a frozen decision protocol first.
